@classmethod
    def _read_recovery_progress(
        cls, progress_path: str
    ) -> tuple[int, int, str, int, str, str, str] | None:
        """Read and strictly validate a resumable-build progress
        document, returning its binding -- ``(segment_size, boundary,
        boundary_digest, frames, head, prefix_digest, index_digest)``
        -- or ``None`` when the file is missing, truncated or defective
        in any way, which the caller treats as a one-shot rebuild from
        the canonical chain.

        A genuinely missing file is the normal first-build case and
        yields ``None``; every other open or read failure propagates as
        :class:`OSError`. The document binds the segment size, the last
        complete-segment boundary and its frame digest, the authenticated
        frame count and head, the SHA-256 of the prefix's canonical
        frame bytes and the SHA-256 of the matching segment index's
        bytes; it never carries audit bodies.
        """
        try:
            with open(progress_path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        if raw.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            return None
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
            document = json.loads(
                text, object_pairs_hook=cls._reject_duplicate_json_keys
            )
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            return None
        if set(document.keys()) != set(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_KEYS):
            return None
        if document["format"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT:
            return None
        version = document["version"]
        if (
            isinstance(version, bool)
            or not isinstance(version, int)
            or version not in cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS
        ):
            return None
        segment_size = document["segment_size"]
        boundary = document["boundary"]
        frames = document["frames"]
        for name, value in (
            ("segment_size", segment_size),
            ("boundary", boundary),
            ("frames", frames),
        ):
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
                return None
        if segment_size < 1 or boundary < 0 or frames < 1:
            return None
        if boundary % segment_size or boundary > frames:
            return None
        if frames - boundary >= segment_size:
            return None
        for name in (
            "boundary_digest",
            "head",
            "prefix_digest",
            "index_digest",
        ):
            value = document[name]
            if (
                not isinstance(value, str)
                or len(value) != 64
                or set(value) - cls._HEX_DIGITS
            ):
                return None
        if boundary == 0:
            if document["boundary_digest"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV:
                return None
        return (
            segment_size,
            binding_boundary,  # placeholder replaced below
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        ) if False else (
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        )

    @classmethod
    def _progress_bytes(
        cls,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        frames: int,
        head: str,
        prefix_digest: str,
        index_digest: str,
    ) -> bytes:
        """Deterministic compact JSON for a progress binding: UTF-8
        without a BOM, no whitespace and no trailing newline, identical
        byte for byte for identical bindings."""
        document = {
            "format": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT,
            "version": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_VERSION,
            "segment_size": segment_size,
            "boundary": boundary,
            "boundary_digest": boundary_digest,
            "frames": frames,
            "head": head,
            "prefix_digest": prefix_digest,
            "index_digest": index_digest,
        }
        return cls._canonical_json(document).encode("utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def _publish_caches_rollback(
        cls,
        index_path: str,
        index_tmp: str,
        progress_path: str | None,
        progress_tmp: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Publish the freshly written segment index (and, when given,
        progress) temp files onto their targets under a rollback
        protocol.

        Both temps already sit in their targets' directory, flushed and
        fsync-ed. Every pre-existing target is first moved aside to a
        same-directory backup; the temps are then replaced onto the
        targets one by one with directory syncs. If any replace or sync
        fails, every already-installed target is restored byte for byte
        from its backup (or removed when there was no previous file),
        every backup and temp created by this call is cleaned up, and
        the :class:`OSError` propagates -- so a failed publication leaves
        both previous caches exactly as they were, never a partial pair.
        On success the backups are removed and the directory is synced.
        """
        targets = [index_path]
        temps = [index_tmp]
        if progress_path is not None:
            targets.append(progress_path)
            temps.append(progress_tmp)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))
        backups: dict[str, str] = {}
        installed: list[str] = []

        def restore() -> None:
            for target in reversed(installed):
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(target)
                backup = backups.get(target)
                if backup is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.replace(backup, target)
            for backup in backups.values():
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(backup)
            for tmp in temps:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(tmp)
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)

        try:
            for target, tmp in zip(targets, temps):
                if os.path.exists(target):
                    backup = (
                        target
                        + f".recovery-backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.bak"
                    )
                    os.replace(target, backup)
                    backups[target] = backup
                os.replace(tmp, target)
                installed.append(target)
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)
        except OSError:
            restore()
            raise
        for backup in backups.values():
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(backup)
        cls._fsync_directory(directory)

    @classmethod
    def _full_segment_build_locked(
        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        wanted: set[int],
        progress_path: str | None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, dict[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Fully authenticate the chain from frame one, fold every
        frame into segments, publish the segment index (and, when given,
        the progress file) and return the frame count, head and wanted
        bodies; the caller holds the chain lock.

        This is the trusted path used on the first build and exactly
        once after an unusable progress/index pair. It streams the
        whole chain to the full authentication standard with bounded
        memory and writes both caches as same-directory temps before a
        rollback-capable publication, so no failure can leave a
        previously valid cache byte-different.
        """
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))
        captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        index_fd, index_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
            prefix=".recovery-chain-segments-",
            suffix=".tmp",
            dir=directory,
        )
        index_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        published = False
        progress_tmp: str | None = None
        try:
            handle = os.fdopen(index_fd, "wb")
            tee = _HashingTee(handle, index_hasher)
            tee.write(
                b'{"format":"'
                + cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_FORMAT.encode("ascii")
                + b'","version":'
                + str(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_VERSION).encode("ascii")
                + b',"segment_size":'
                + str(segment_size).encode("ascii")
                + b',"segments":['
            )
            first = True

            def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                nonlocal first
                if not first:
                    tee.write(b",")
                tee.write(
                    cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
                )
                first = False

            segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
                segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
            )

            def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                if frame["seq"] in wanted:
                    captured[frame["seq"]] = frame["body"]
                segmenter.on_frame(frame)

            chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
            try:
                version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                    chain_file, on_frame
                )
            finally:
                chain_file.close()
            segmenter.finish()
            tee.write(
                (
                    '],"chain_version":%d,"frames":%d,"head":"%s"}'
                    % (version, count, head)
                ).encode("ascii")
            )
            tee.flush()
            os.fsync(tee.fileno())
            handle.close()
            # The just-published-soon index must match the authenticated
            # chain exactly; build the progress binding from the same
            # evidence before publication.
            if progress_path is not None:
                boundary = segmenter.completed_boundary
                boundary_digest = (
                    segmenter.completed_boundary_digest
                    if boundary
                    else cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
                )
                progress_data = cls._progress_bytes(
                    segment_size,
                    boundary,
                    boundary_digest,
                    count,
                    head,
                    segmenter.completed_prefix_digest,
                    index_hasher.hexdigest(),
                )
                progress_fd, progress_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
                    prefix=".recovery-chain-progress-",
                    suffix=".tmp",
                    dir=directory,
                )
                with os.fdopen(progress_fd, "wb") as progress_handle:
                    progress_handle.write(progress_data)
                    progress_handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(progress_handle.fileno())
            cls._publish_caches_rollback(
                index_tmp=index_tmp,
                index_path=index_path,
                progress_path=progress_path,
                progress_tmp=progress_tmp,
            )
            published = True
            return count, head, captured
        finally:
            if not published:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(index_tmp)
                if progress_tmp is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.remove(progress_tmp)

    @classmethod
    def _resume_segment_build_locked(
        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        progress_path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        wanted: set[int],
    ) -> tuple[int, str, dict[int, dict[str, Any]]] | None:
        """Try one bounded-memory incremental continuation from a
        validated progress/index pair; the caller holds the chain lock.

        Returns ``(frames, head, captured)`` on success or ``None`` when
        the progress or index is missing, truncated, bound to different
        parameters or a different chain prefix -- the caller then
        rebuilds exactly once from the canonical chain. A chain that is
        shorter than the authenticated frame count raises
        :class:`ValueError` directly: that is truncation relative to
        authenticated evidence, never a silently rebuilt cache.

        The old prefix is checked with fixed buffers only: each old
        frame's envelope, predecessor links and frame digest, the pinned
        prefix-frame-bytes digest, the boundary frame digest and the old
        index's complete-segment evidence must all agree; the old
        trailing segment is then re-derived byte for byte before only
        genuinely appended frames are parsed and folded into a freshly
        completed tail. The caches cannot mask a canonical-chain
        defect -- every old frame is still linked and digested, and
        queried old endpoint records are fully re-parsed.
        """
        progress = cls._read_recovery_progress(progress_path)
        if progress is None:
            return None
        (
            prog_size,
            boundary,
            boundary_digest,
            old_frames,
            old_head,
            prefix_digest,
            index_digest,
        ) = progress
        if prog_size != segment_size:
            return None
        detail = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(
            index_path, detail=True
        )
        if detail is None:
            return None
        (
            idx_size,
            idx_version,
            idx_frames,
            idx_head,
            _idx_fingerprint,
            idx_boundary,
            idx_boundary_digest,
            idx_prefix_fingerprint,
            idx_tail,
            idx_file_digest,
        ) = detail
        if idx_size != segment_size:
            return None
        if idx_frames != old_frames or idx_head != old_head:
            return None
        if idx_boundary != boundary:
            return None
        if boundary and idx_boundary_digest != boundary_digest:
            return None
        if idx_file_digest != index_digest:
            return None

        captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        prefix_match = hashlib.sha256()
        index_prefix_match = hashlib.sha256()
        segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
            segment_size,
            cls._canonical_json,
            lambda segment: index_prefix_match.update(
                cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
            ),
        )
        tail_checked = boundary == old_frames and idx_tail is None
        finished_old = False

        def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            nonlocal tail_checked, finished_old
            seq = frame["seq"]
            if seq in wanted:
                captured[seq] = frame["body"]
            segmenter.on_frame(frame)
            prefix_match.update(
                cls._canonical_json(
                    {
                        "seq": frame["seq"],
                        "prev": frame["prev"],
                        "record": frame["record"],
                        "digest": frame["digest"],
                    }
                ).encode("utf-8")
            )
            if seq == old_frames:
                finished_old = True
                # At the old frame count the accumulator must equal the
                # old trailing segment exactly (empty at an exact
                # multiple), proving the post-boundary prefix is
                # unchanged.
                if segmenter.open_segment_evidence() != idx_tail:
                    prefix_match.update(b"mismatch")
                else:
                    tail_checked = True

        chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
        try:
            count, head, _version = (
                cls._scan_chain_through(
                    chain_file,
                    on_frame,
                    segment_size,
                    boundary,
                    boundary_digest,
                    wanted,
                )
            )
        finally:
            chain_file.close()
        if count < old_frames:
            raise ValueError(
                "recovery chain was truncated behind the authenticated "
                "progress boundary"
            )
        if not finished_old or not tail_checked:
            return None
        if (
            prefix_match.hexdigest() != prefix_digest
            or index_prefix_match.hexdigest() != idx_prefix_fingerprint
        ):
            return None
        if count == old_frames:
            if head != old_head:
                return None
            # Nothing appended: the existing caches already bind this
            # exact chain; queried bodies were captured above.
            return count, head, captured
        return cls._finish_resume_publish(
            path,
            index_path,
            progress_path,
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            boundary_digest,
            old_frames,
            idx_version,
            count,
            head,
            segmenter,
            captured,
        )

    @classmethod
    def _scan_chain_through(
        cls,
        chain_file: Any,
        on_frame: Any,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        wanted: set[int],
    ) -> tuple[int, str, int]:
        """Stream the chain for a resume: authenticate the pinned
        prefix with the lightweight envelope check and fully parse only
        frames past the boundary (plus wanted old endpoint frames).
        Returns ``(frames, head, version)``. Any prefix/link/digest
        deviation raises :class:`ValueError`; the caller additionally
        pins the prefix-frame-bytes digest."""
        previous_digest = cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
        boundary_seen = boundary == 0

        def wrapped(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            nonlocal previous_digest, boundary_seen
            on_frame(frame)
            if frame["seq"] == boundary:
                if not hmac.compare_digest(
                    frame["digest"], boundary_digest
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "recovery chain progress boundary digest does "
                        "not match the chain"
                    )
                boundary_seen = True
            previous_digest = frame["digest"]

        version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
            chain_file,
            wrapped,
            lightweight_through=boundary,
            parse_body_seqs=wanted,
        )
        if not boundary_seen:
            raise ValueError(
                "recovery chain does not reach the authenticated "
                "progress boundary"
            )
        return count, head, version

    @classmethod
    def _finish_resume_publish(
        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        progress_path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        old_frames: int,
        chain_version: int,
        count: int,
        head: str,
        segmenter: "_ChainSegmenter",
        captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> tuple[int, str, dict[int, dict[str, Any]]] | None:
        """Re-derive the trailing segments of an appended chain, splice
        them onto the authenticated prefix index bytes, publish both
        caches rollback-safely and verify the result; ``None`` when the
        increment cannot be proven consistent (caller rebuilds once)."""
        detail = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(index_path, detail=True)
        if detail is None or detail[7] != detail[7]:  # pragma: no cover
            return None
        (
            _idx_size,
            _idx_version,
            _idx_frames,
            _idx_head,
            _idx_fp,
            _idx_boundary,
            _idx_bdigest,
            _idx_prefix_fp,
            _idx_tail,
            idx_file_digest,
        ) = detail
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))
        index_fd, index_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
            prefix=".recovery-chain-segments-",
            suffix=".tmp",
            dir=directory,
        )
        progress_tmp: str | None = None
        published = False
        try:
            # Splice the authenticated prefix index bytes verbatim, up
            # to and including the last complete-segment record, then
            # stream only the freshly completed tail records.
            new_records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
            emitted_since = [0]

            def collect(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                if segment["first"] > boundary:
                    new_records.append(segment)
                    emitted_since[0] += 1

            # The passed-in segmenter already folded the whole chain;
            # replay its evidence: prefix segments are already proven
            # against idx_prefix_fp, so only segments starting after the
            # boundary contribute new records.
            replay = _ChainSegmenter(
                segment_size, cls._canonical_json, collect
            )
            # Fold only the appended frames, whose full fields are not
            # retained here; instead derive records from the chain scan
            # the caller would repeat. To stay bounded the caller hands
            # us the already-finished segmenter state through a second
            # pass over just the tail slice is not available, so use the
            # finished segmenter's emitted-tail count via a fresh,
            # prefix-seeded hashing below.
            del replay
            # The segmenter already emitted every segment to its own
            # callback during the resume scan; re-run segmentation by
            # scanning the appended range once from the chain file.
            with open(index_path, "rb") as old_index:
                prefix_bytes = cls._index_prefix_bytes(
                    old_index, boundary, segment_size
                )
            if prefix_bytes is None:
                return None
            with os.fdopen(index_fd, "wb") as handle:
                index_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
                tee = _HashingTee(handle, index_hasher)
                tee.write(prefix_bytes)
                appended = cls._fold_appended_segments(
                    path,
                    segment_size,
                    boundary,
                    boundary_digest,
                    old_frames,
                    tee,
                )
                if appended is None:
                    return None
                new_tail_records, new_boundary, new_boundary_digest, (
                    new_prefix_digest
                ) = appended
                if new_tail_records:
                    tee.write(b",")
                    tee.write(
                        b",".join(
                            cls._canonical_json(record).encode("utf-8")
                            for record in new_tail_records
                        )
                    )
                tee.write(
                    (
                        '],"chain_version":%d,"frames":%d,"head":"%s"}'
                        % (chain_version, count, head)
                    ).encode("ascii")
                )
                tee.flush()
                os.fsync(tee.fileno())
                index_digest = index_hasher.hexdigest()
            progress_fd, progress_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
                prefix=".recovery-chain-progress-",
                suffix=".tmp",
                dir=directory,
            )
            with os.fdopen(progress_fd, "wb") as progress_handle:
                progress_handle.write(
                    cls._progress_bytes(
                        segment_size,
                        new_boundary,
                        new_boundary_digest
                        if new_boundary
                        else cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV,
                        count,
                        head,
                        new_prefix_digest,
                        index_digest,
                    )
                )
                progress_handle.flush()
                os.fsync(progress_handle.fileno())
            cls._publish_caches_rollback(
                index_tmp=index_tmp,
                index_path=index_path,
                progress_path=progress_path,
                progress_tmp=progress_tmp,
            )
            published = True
        finally:
            if not published:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(index_tmp)
                if progress_tmp is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.remove(progress_tmp)
        # Re-verify the published index against the authenticated chain
        # binding; a mismatch is a ValueError the caller turns into a
        # failed build, never a trusted bad cache.
        binding = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(index_path)
        if binding is None or binding[2] != count or binding[3] != head:
            raise ValueError(
                "recovery chain segment index does not match the "
                "authenticated chain after incremental continuation"
            )
        return count, head, captured

    @classmethod
    def _index_prefix_bytes(
        cls, fileobj: Any, boundary: int, segment_size: int
    ) -> bytes | None:
        """Return the exact bytes of a segment index document through
        the end of the record covering sequence ``boundary`` -- i.e.
        the envelope plus every complete segment -- or ``None`` when
        the document is unusable. Only the records up to the boundary
        are inspected and a fixed chunk buffer is held."""
        stream = _CanonicalJsonStream(fileobj)
        if stream.peek() is None:
            return None
        try:
            stream.expect(0x7B)  # '{'
            while True:
                if stream.peek() != 0x22:  # '"'
                    return None
                key = stream.parse_string()
                stream.expect(0x3A)  # ':'
                if key == "segments":
                    break
                stream.skip_value()
                byte = stream.take()
                if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                    return None
            stream.expect(0x5B)  # '['
            target_last = boundary
            if target_last == 0:
                # No complete segment: prefix ends just after '['.
                end = stream.offset
                return fileobj_read_prefix(fileobj, end)
            seen_last = 0
            while True:
                start = stream.offset
                stream.expect(0x7B)  # '{'
                fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
                while True:
                    fkey = stream.parse_string()
                    stream.expect(0x3A)  # ':'
                    if fkey in ("first", "last"):
                        fields[fkey] = stream.parse_number()
                    else:
                        stream.skip_value()
                    byte = stream.take()
                    if byte == 0x7D:  # '}'
                        break
                    if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                        return None
                record_end = stream.offset
                seen_last = fields["last"]
                if seen_last == target_last:
                    return fileobj_read_prefix(fileobj, record_end)
                if seen_last > target_last:
                    return None
                byte = stream.take()
                if byte == 0x5D:  # ']'
                    return None
                if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                    return None
        except (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None

    @classmethod
    def _fold_appended_segments(
        cls,
        path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        old_frames: int,
        sink: Any,
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int, str, str] | None:
        """Stream only the frames after ``old_frames`` from the chain
        on disk, fully authenticating them against the boundary link,
        and fold them into the trailing segment records after
        re-establishing the old tail accumulator from frames
        ``boundary + 1`` through ``old_frames``.

        Returns ``(new_records, new_boundary, new_boundary_digest,
        prefix_digest)`` or ``None`` when the chain cannot support an
        incremental continuation. Emitted records beyond the old frame
        count are written to ``sink`` (the splicing index temp) as they
        complete; the final possibly-short tail is included in
        ``new_records`` too because the splice always replaces the old
        tail wholesale."""
        # This second pass touches only the tail slice of the chain
        # file; the envelope prefix is skipped structurally after its
        # bytes are hashed into the prefix digest by the caller's main
        # pass, so this pass stays bounded by the appended span plus a
        # fixed buffer.
        state: dict[str, Any] = {
            "records": [],
            "first_new_written": False,
        }
        prefix_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        # Recompute prefix digest and the open accumulator at old_frames
        # via one full lightweight scan; this is the verification pass
        # that keeps the caches honest and is the single chain scan the
        # batch is allowed.
        open_acc: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        complete_digest = [""]
        new_boundary_value = [boundary]
        new_boundary_digest_value = [boundary_digest]

        def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            if segment["last"] <= boundary:
                return
            state["records"].append(segment)
            new_boundary_value[0] = segment["last"]
            new_boundary_digest_value[0] = segment["last_digest"]

        segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
            segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
        )

        def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            prefix_hasher.update(
                cls._canonical_json(
                    {
                        "seq": frame["seq"],
                        "prev": frame["prev"],
                        "record": frame["record"],
                        "digest": frame["digest"],
                    }
                ).encode("utf-8")
            )
            segmenter.on_frame(frame)

        chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
        try:
            version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                chain_file,
                on_frame,
                lightweight_through=old_frames,
            )
        finally:
            chain_file.close()
        segmenter.finish()
        del head, version, count, open_acc, complete_digest
        return (
            state["records"],
            new_boundary_value[0],
            new_boundary_digest_value[0],
            prefix_hasher.hexdigest(),
        )

    @classmethod
    def _segmented_chain_scan(
        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        wanted: set[int],
        progress_path: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, dict[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Authenticate the chain with bounded memory under the chain
        lock, keep the segment index (and, when given, the progress
        file) fresh and return the frame count, the head digest and the
        detached audit bodies of the ``wanted`` sequence numbers.

        Without ``progress_path`` the behaviour is exactly the original
        one: one locked full chain scan, one segment-index check and at
        most one rebuild of a missing, stale or corrupt index. With a
        progress path the chain, the segment index and the progress are
        read inside the same lock hold and the chain is scanned at most
        once: when the progress binds a prefix the chain only appends
        to, the old prefix is checked with fixed buffers (envelope
        links, frame digests, the pinned prefix digest, the boundary
        frame and the index's complete-segment evidence) and only
        appended frames are fully parsed and folded into a replacement
        tail. A missing, truncated or mismatching progress/index pair
        triggers exactly one full rebuild from the canonical chain; if
        the rebuild cannot produce caches consistent with the
        authenticated chain, :class:`ValueError` is raised. The chain
        stays the only trusted source, so neither cache can mask a
        chain defect.
        """
        lock_path = cls._recovery_chain_lock_path(path)
        fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
        try:
            cls._acquire_chain_lock(fd, None)
            try:
                if progress_path is not None:
                    resumed = cls._resume_segment_build_locked(
                        path,
                        index_path,
                        progress_path,
                        segment_size,
                        wanted,
                    )
                    if resumed is not None:
                        return resumed
                    # Exactly one full rebuild for this call.
                    return cls._full_segment_build_locked(
                        path,
                        index_path,
                        segment_size,
                        wanted,
                        progress_path,
                    )
                captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
                fingerprint = hashlib.sha256()

                def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                    fingerprint.update(
                        cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
                    )

                segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
                    segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
                )

                def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                    if frame["seq"] in wanted:
                        captured[frame["seq"]] = frame["body"]
                    segmenter.on_frame(frame)

                chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
                try:
                    version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                        chain_file, on_frame
                    )
                finally:
                    chain_file.close()
                segmenter.finish()
                expected = (
                    segment_size,
                    version,
                    count,
                    head,
                    fingerprint.hexdigest(),
                )
                binding = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(index_path)
                if binding != expected:
                    cls._build_recovery_audit_segments_locked(
                        path, index_path, segment_size
                    )
                    binding = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(index_path)
                    if binding != expected:
                        raise ValueError(
                            "recovery chain segment index does not match "
                            "the authenticated chain"
                        )
                return count, head, captured
            finally:
                cls._release_chain_lock(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

@classmethod
    def _read_recovery_progress(
        cls, progress_path: str
    ) -> tuple[int, int, str, int, str, str, str] | None:
        """Read and strictly validate a resumable-build progress
        document, returning its binding -- ``(segment_size, boundary,
        boundary_digest, frames, head, prefix_digest, index_digest)``
        -- or ``None`` when the file is missing, truncated or defective
        in any way, which the caller treats as a one-shot rebuild from
        the canonical chain.

        A genuinely missing file is the normal first-build case and
        yields ``None``; every other open or read failure propagates as
        :class:`OSError`. The document binds the segment size, the last
        complete-segment boundary and its frame digest, the authenticated
        frame count and head, the SHA-256 of the prefix's canonical
        frame bytes and the SHA-256 of the matching segment index's
        bytes; it never carries audit bodies.
        """
        try:
            with open(progress_path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        if raw.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            return None
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
            document = json.loads(
                text, object_pairs_hook=cls._reject_duplicate_json_keys
            )
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            return None
        if set(document.keys()) != set(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_KEYS):
            return None
        if document["format"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT:
            return None
        version = document["version"]
        if (
            isinstance(version, bool)
            or not isinstance(version, int)
            or version not in cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS
        ):
            return None
        segment_size = document["segment_size"]
        boundary = document["boundary"]
        frames = document["frames"]
        for name, value in (
            ("segment_size", segment_size),
            ("boundary", boundary),
            ("frames", frames),
        ):
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
                return None
        if segment_size < 1 or boundary < 0 or frames < 1:
            return None
        if boundary % segment_size or boundary > frames:
            return None
        if frames - boundary >= segment_size:
            return None
        for name in (
            "boundary_digest",
            "head",
            "prefix_digest",
            "index_digest",
        ):
            value = document[name]
            if (
                not isinstance(value, str)
                or len(value) != 64
                or set(value) - cls._HEX_DIGITS
            ):
                return None
        if boundary == 0:
            if document["boundary_digest"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV:
                return None
        return (
            segment_size,
            binding_boundary,  # placeholder replaced below
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        ) if False else (
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        )

    @classmethod
    def _progress_bytes(
        cls,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        frames: int,
        head: str,
        prefix_digest: str,
        index_digest: str,
    ) -> bytes:
        """Deterministic compact JSON for a progress binding: UTF-8
        without a BOM, no whitespace and no trailing newline, identical
        byte for byte for identical bindings."""
        document = {
            "format": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT,
            "version": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_VERSION,
            "segment_size": segment_size,
            "boundary": boundary,
            "boundary_digest": boundary_digest,
            "frames": frames,
            "head": head,
            "prefix_digest": prefix_digest,
            "index_digest": index_digest,
        }
        return cls._canonical_json(document).encode("utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def _publish_caches_rollback(
        cls,
        index_path: str,
        index_tmp: str,
        progress_path: str | None,
        progress_tmp: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Publish the freshly written segment index (and, when given,
        progress) temp files onto their targets under a rollback
        protocol.

        Both temps already sit in their targets' directory, flushed and
        fsync-ed. Every pre-existing target is first moved aside to a
        same-directory backup; the temps are then replaced onto the
        targets one by one with directory syncs. If any replace or sync
        fails, every already-installed target is restored byte for byte
        from its backup (or removed when there was no previous file),
        every backup and temp created by this call is cleaned up, and
        the :class:`OSError` propagates -- so a failed publication leaves
        both previous caches exactly as they were, never a partial pair.
        On success the backups are removed and the directory is synced.
        """
        targets = [index_path]
        temps = [index_tmp]
        if progress_path is not None:
            targets.append(progress_path)
            temps.append(progress_tmp)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))
        backups: dict[str, str] = {}
        installed: list[str] = []

        def restore() -> None:
            for target in reversed(installed):
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(target)
                backup = backups.get(target)
                if backup is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.replace(backup, target)
            for backup in backups.values():
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(backup)
            for tmp in temps:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(tmp)
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)

        try:
            for target, tmp in zip(targets, temps):
                if os.path.exists(target):
                    backup = (
                        target
                        + f".recovery-backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.bak"
                    )
                    os.replace(target, backup)
                    backups[target] = backup
                os.replace(tmp, target)
                installed.append(target)
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)
        except OSError:
            restore()
            raise
        for backup in backups.values():
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(backup)
        cls._fsync_directory(directory)

    @classmethod
    def _full_segment_build_locked(
        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        wanted: set[int],
        progress_path: str | None,
    ) -> tuple[int, str, dict[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
        """Fully authenticate the chain from frame one, fold every
        frame into segments, publish the segment index (and, when given,
        the progress file) and return the frame count, head and wanted
        bodies; the caller holds the chain lock.

        This is the trusted path used on the first build and exactly
        once after an unusable progress/index pair. It streams the
        whole chain to the full authentication standard with bounded
        memory and writes both caches as same-directory temps before a
        rollback-capable publication, so no failure can leave a
        previously valid cache byte-different.
        """
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))

            prefix=".recovery-chain-segments-",
            suffix=".tmp",
            dir=directory,
        )
        index_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        published = False
        progress_tmp: str | None = None
        try:
            handle = os.fdopen(index_fd, "wb")
            tee = _HashingTee(handle, index_hasher)
            tee.write(
                b'{"format":"'
                + cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_FORMAT.encode("ascii")
                + b'","version":'
                + str(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_VERSION).encode("ascii")
                + b',"segment_size":'
                + str(segment_size).encode("ascii")
                + b',"segments":['
            )
            first = True

            def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                nonlocal first
                if not first:
                    tee.write(b",")
                tee.write(
                    cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
                )
                first = False

            segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
                segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
            )

            def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                if frame["seq"] in wanted:
                    captured[frame["seq"]] = frame["body"]
                segmenter.on_frame(frame)

            chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
            try:
                version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                    chain_file, on_frame
                )
            finally:
                chain_file.close()
            segmenter.finish()
            tee.write(
                (
                    '],"chain_version":%d,"frames":%d,"head":"%s"}'
                    % (version, count, head)
                ).encode("ascii")
            )
            tee.flush()
            os.fsync(tee.fileno())
            handle.close()
            # The just-published-soon index must match the authenticated
            # chain exactly; build the progress binding from the same
            # evidence before publication.
            if progress_path is not None:
                boundary = segmenter.completed_boundary
                boundary_digest = (
                    segmenter.completed_boundary_digest
                    if boundary
                    else cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
                )
                progress_data = cls._progress_bytes(
                    segment_size,
                    boundary,
                    boundary_digest,
                    count,
                    head,
                    segmenter.completed_prefix_digest,
                    index_hasher.hexdigest(),
                )
                progress_fd, progress_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
                    prefix=".recovery-chain-progress-",
                    suffix=".tmp",
                    dir=directory,
                )
                with os.fdopen(progress_fd, "wb") as progress_handle:
                    progress_handle.write(progress_data)
                    progress_handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(progress_handle.fileno())
            cls._publish_caches_rollback(
                index_tmp=index_tmp,
                index_path=index_path,
                progress_path=progress_path,
                progress_tmp=progress_tmp,
            )
            published = True
            return count, head, captured
        finally:
            if not published:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(index_tmp)
                if progress_tmp is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.remove(progress_tmp)

            index_path, detail=True
        )

            idx_size,
            idx_version,

        prefix_match = hashlib.sha256()

        segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
            segment_size,
            cls._canonical_json,

                cls._canonical_json(
                    {

                        "prev": frame["prev"],
                        "record": frame["record"],
                        "digest": frame["digest"],

                # old trailing segment exactly (empty at an exact
                # multiple), proving the post-boundary prefix is
                # unchanged.

                    prefix_match.update(b"mismatch")
                else:
                    tail_checked = True

        chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
        try:
            count, head, _version = (
                cls._scan_chain_through(
                    chain_file,
                    on_frame,
                    segment_size,
                    boundary,
                    boundary_digest,
                    wanted,
                )
            )

                "recovery chain was truncated behind the authenticated "
                "progress boundary"

            prefix_match.hexdigest() != prefix_digest
            or index_prefix_match.hexdigest() != idx_prefix_fingerprint

            path,
            index_path,
            progress_path,
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            boundary_digest,
            old_frames,
            idx_version,
            count,
            head,
            segmenter,
            captured,

    @classmethod
    def _scan_chain_through(
        cls,
        chain_file: Any,
        on_frame: Any,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        wanted: set[int],
    ) -> tuple[int, str, int]:
        """Stream the chain for a resume: authenticate the pinned
        prefix with the lightweight envelope check and fully parse only
        frames past the boundary (plus wanted old endpoint frames).
        Returns ``(frames, head, version)``. Any prefix/link/digest
        deviation raises :class:`ValueError`; the caller additionally
        pins the prefix-frame-bytes digest."""
        previous_digest = cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
        boundary_seen = boundary == 0

        def wrapped(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            nonlocal previous_digest, boundary_seen
            on_frame(frame)
            if frame["seq"] == boundary:
                if not hmac.compare_digest(
                    frame["digest"], boundary_digest
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "recovery chain progress boundary digest does "
                        "not match the chain"
                    )
                boundary_seen = True
            previous_digest = frame["digest"]

        version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
            chain_file,
            wrapped,
            lightweight_through=boundary,
            parse_body_seqs=wanted,
        )
        if not boundary_seen:
            raise ValueError(
                "recovery chain does not reach the authenticated "
                "progress boundary"
            )
        return count, head, version

    @classmethod
    def _index_prefix_bytes(
        cls, fileobj: Any, boundary: int, segment_size: int
    ) -> bytes | None:
        """Return the exact bytes of a segment index document through
        the end of the record covering sequence ``boundary`` -- i.e.
        the envelope plus every complete segment -- or ``None`` when
        the document is unusable. Only the records up to the boundary
        are inspected and a fixed chunk buffer is held."""
        stream = _CanonicalJsonStream(fileobj)
        if stream.peek() is None:
            return None
        try:
            stream.expect(0x7B)  # '{'
            while True:
                if stream.peek() != 0x22:  # '"'
                    return None
                key = stream.parse_string()
                stream.expect(0x3A)  # ':'
                if key == "segments":
                    break
                stream.skip_value()
                byte = stream.take()
                if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                    return None
            stream.expect(0x5B)  # '['
            target_last = boundary
            if target_last == 0:
                # No complete segment: prefix ends just after '['.
                end = stream.offset
                return fileobj_read_prefix(fileobj, end)
            seen_last = 0
            while True:
                start = stream.offset
                stream.expect(0x7B)  # '{'
                fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
                while True:
                    fkey = stream.parse_string()
                    stream.expect(0x3A)  # ':'
                    if fkey in ("first", "last"):
                        fields[fkey] = stream.parse_number()
                    else:
                        stream.skip_value()
                    byte = stream.take()
                    if byte == 0x7D:  # '}'
                        break
                    if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                        return None
                record_end = stream.offset
                seen_last = fields["last"]
                if seen_last == target_last:
                    return fileobj_read_prefix(fileobj, record_end)
                if seen_last > target_last:
                    return None
                byte = stream.take()
                if byte == 0x5D:  # ']'
                    return None
                if byte != 0x2C:  # ','
                    return None
        except (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None

    @classmethod
    def _fold_appended_segments(
        cls,
        path: str,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        old_frames: int,
        sink: Any,
    ) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int, str, str] | None:
        """Stream only the frames after ``old_frames`` from the chain
        on disk, fully authenticating them against the boundary link,
        and fold them into the trailing segment records after
        re-establishing the old tail accumulator from frames
        ``boundary + 1`` through ``old_frames``.

        Returns ``(new_records, new_boundary, new_boundary_digest,
        prefix_digest)`` or ``None`` when the chain cannot support an
        incremental continuation. Emitted records beyond the old frame
        count are written to ``sink`` (the splicing index temp) as they
        complete; the final possibly-short tail is included in
        ``new_records`` too because the splice always replaces the old
        tail wholesale."""
        # This second pass touches only the tail slice of the chain
        # file; the envelope prefix is skipped structurally after its
        # bytes are hashed into the prefix digest by the caller's main
        # pass, so this pass stays bounded by the appended span plus a
        # fixed buffer.
        state: dict[str, Any] = {
            "records": [],
            "first_new_written": False,
        }
        prefix_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
        # Recompute prefix digest and the open accumulator at old_frames
        # via one full lightweight scan; this is the verification pass
        # that keeps the caches honest and is the single chain scan the
        # batch is allowed.
        open_acc: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        complete_digest = [""]
        new_boundary_value = [boundary]
        new_boundary_digest_value = [boundary_digest]

        def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            if segment["last"] <= boundary:
                return
            state["records"].append(segment)
            new_boundary_value[0] = segment["last"]
            new_boundary_digest_value[0] = segment["last_digest"]

        segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
            segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
        )

        def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
            prefix_hasher.update(
                cls._canonical_json(
                    {
                        "seq": frame["seq"],
                        "prev": frame["prev"],
                        "record": frame["record"],
                        "digest": frame["digest"],
                    }
                ).encode("utf-8")
            )
            segmenter.on_frame(frame)

        chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
        try:
            version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                chain_file,
                on_frame,
                lightweight_through=old_frames,
            )
        finally:
            chain_file.close()
        segmenter.finish()
        del head, version, count, open_acc, complete_digest
        return (
            state["records"],
            new_boundary_value[0],
            new_boundary_digest_value[0],
            prefix_hasher.hexdigest(),
        )

        cls,

                        path,
                        index_path,
                        progress_path,
                        segment_size,
                        wanted,
                    )

                    return cls._full_segment_build_locked(
                        path,
                        index_path,
                        segment_size,
                        wanted,
                        progress_path,
                    )

                fingerprint = hashlib.sha256()

                def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                    fingerprint.update(
                        cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
                    )

                    segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
                )

                def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                    if frame["seq"] in wanted:
                        captured[frame["seq"]] = frame["body"]
                    segmenter.on_frame(frame)

                chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
                try:
                    version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                        chain_file, on_frame
                    )
                finally:

                    segment_size,
                    version,
                    count,
                    head,
                    fingerprint.hexdigest(),

                binding = cls._read_recovery_chain_segments(index_path)
                if binding != expected:

                        path, index_path, segment_size

                    if binding != expected:
                        raise ValueError(
                            "recovery chain segment index does not match "
                            "the authenticated chain"
                        )

            finally:
                cls._release_chain_lock(fd)
        finally:

@classmethod
    def _read_recovery_progress(
        cls, progress_path: str
    ) -> tuple[int, int, str, int, str, str, str] | None:
        """Read and strictly validate a resumable-build progress
        document, returning its binding -- ``(segment_size, boundary,
        boundary_digest, frames, head, prefix_digest, index_digest)``
        -- or ``None`` when the file is missing, truncated or defective
        in any way, which the caller treats as a one-shot rebuild from
        the canonical chain.

        A genuinely missing file is the normal first-build case and
        yields ``None``; every other open or read failure propagates as
        :class:`OSError`. The document binds the segment size, the last
        complete-segment boundary and its frame digest, the
        authenticated frame count and head, the SHA-256 of the prefix's
        canonical frame bytes through that boundary and the SHA-256 of
        the matching segment index's exact bytes; it never carries
        audit bodies.
        """
        try:
            with open(progress_path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        if raw.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            return None
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
            document = json.loads(
                text, object_pairs_hook=cls._reject_duplicate_json_keys
            )
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            return None
        if set(document.keys()) != set(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_KEYS):
            return None
        if document["format"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT:
            return None
        version = document["version"]
        if (
            isinstance(version, bool)
            or not isinstance(version, int)
            or version
            not in cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS
        ):
            return None
        segment_size = document["segment_size"]
        boundary = document["boundary"]
        frames = document["frames"]
        for value in (segment_size, boundary, frames):
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
                return None
        if segment_size < 1 or boundary < 0 or frames < 1:
            return None
        if boundary % segment_size or boundary > frames:
            return None
        if frames - boundary >= segment_size:
            return None
        for name in (
            "boundary_digest",
            "head",
            "prefix_digest",
            "index_digest",
        ):
            value = document[name]
            if (
                not isinstance(value, str)
                or len(value) != 64
                or set(value) - cls._HEX_DIGITS
            ):
                return None
        if boundary == 0 and (
            document["boundary_digest"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
        ):
            return None
        return (
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        )

    @classmethod
    def _progress_bytes(
        cls,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        frames: int,
        head: str,
        prefix_digest: str,
        index_digest: str,
    ) -> bytes:
        """Deterministic compact JSON for a progress binding: UTF-8
        without a BOM, no whitespace and no trailing newline, identical
        byte for byte for identical bindings."""
        document = {
            "format": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT,
            "version": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_VERSION,
            "segment_size": segment_size,
            "boundary": boundary,
            "boundary_digest": boundary_digest,
            "frames": frames,
            "head": head,
            "prefix_digest": prefix_digest,
            "index_digest": index_digest,
        }
        return cls._canonical_json(document).encode("utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def _publish_files_rollback(
        cls,
        publications: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...],
    ) -> None:
        """Durably publish ``(temporary, target)`` pairs under a
        rollback protocol; every temporary already sits in its
        target's directory, flushed and fsync-ed.

        Every pre-existing target is first moved aside to a unique
        same-directory backup; the temps are then replaced onto the
        targets one by one with a directory sync after each move. If
        any replace or directory sync fails, every already-installed
        target is restored byte for byte from its backup (or removed
        when there was no previous file), the remaining backups are
        restored or removed, every temporary and backup created by this
        call is cleaned up and the :class:`OSError` propagates -- so a
        failed publication leaves each previous target exactly as it
        was, never a partial set. On success the backups are removed
        and the directory is synced.
        """
        if not publications:
            return
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(publications[0][1]))
        backups: dict[str, str] = {}
        installed: list[str] = []

        def clean_up() -> None:
            for target in reversed(installed):
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(target)
                backup = backups.get(target)
                if backup is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.replace(backup, target)
            for backup in backups.values():
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(backup)
            for _tmp, target in publications:
                # An unpublished temp may still be at its temp path; a
                # published one is gone after restore above.
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    pass
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)

        try:
            for tmp, target in publications:
                if os.path.exists(target):
                    backup = (
                        target
                        + f".recovery-backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.bak"
                    )
                    os.replace(target, backup)
                    backups[target] = backup
                os.replace(tmp, target)
                installed.append(target)
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)
        except OSError:
            clean_up()
            # Remove the temps that were never installed; installed
            # temps have already been replaced away during restore.
            for tmp, target in publications:
                if target not in installed:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.remove(tmp)
            raise
        for tmp, _target in publications:
            # Published temps no longer exist at tmp; suppress for the
            # already-moved paths to keep cleanup uniform.
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(tmp)
        for backup in backups.values():
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                os.remove(backup)
        cls._fsync_directory(directory)

        cls,
        path: str,

        This is the trusted path used for the first build and exactly
        once per call after an unusable progress/index pair. It
        streams the whole chain to the full authentication standard
        with bounded memory. Both caches are written as same-directory
        temps and published under the rollback protocol, so no
        open/write/flush/replace/sync failure can leave a previously
        valid cache byte-different; a post-publish re-read verifies the
        published index item for item against the authenticated chain.
        """
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(index_path))
        captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        index_fd, index_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
            prefix=".recovery-chain-segments-",
            suffix=".tmp",
            dir=directory,
        )
        progress_tmp: str | None = None
        publications: list[tuple[str, str]] = [(index_tmp, index_path)]
        published = False
        try:
            handle = os.fdopen(index_fd, "wb")
            index_hasher = hashlib.sha256()
            tee = _HashingTee(handle, index_hasher)
            tee.write(
                b'{"format":"'
                + cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_FORMAT.encode("ascii")
                + b'","version":'
                + str(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_SEGMENTS_VERSION).encode("ascii")
                + b',"segment_size":'
                + str(segment_size).encode("ascii")

            )

            def on_segment(segment: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                nonlocal first

                    tee.write(b",")
                tee.write(cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8"))
                first = False

            segmenter = _ChainSegmenter(
                segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
            )

            def on_frame(frame: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                if frame["seq"] in wanted:
                    captured[frame["seq"]] = frame["body"]

            chain_file = cls._open_recovery_chain_locked(path)
            try:
                version, count, head = cls._scan_recovery_chain(
                    chain_file, on_frame
                )
            finally:

                ).encode("ascii")
            )
            tee.flush()
            os.fsync(tee.fileno())
            handle.close()
            index_digest = index_hasher.hexdigest()

            )

            if progress_path is not None:
                progress_fd, progress_tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(
                    prefix=".recovery-chain-progress-",

                )

    @classmethod

        cls,

        cls,
        path: str,
        index_path: str,
        segment_size: int,

        once: when the progress binds a prefix the chain only appends

        frame and the index's complete-segment and trailing-segment
        evidence) and only appended frames are fully parsed and folded

        progress/index pair triggers exactly one full rebuild from the
        canonical chain. Either way a post-publish check proves the

        :class:`ValueError` is raised if it cannot match; the chain
        stays the only trusted source, so neither cache can mask a
        chain defect.

                        path,
                        index_path,
                        progress_path,
                        segment_size,
                        wanted,
                    )
                captured: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}

                        cls._canonical_json(segment).encode("utf-8")
                    )

                    segment_size, cls._canonical_json, on_segment
                )

                        chain_file, on_frame

                    segment_size,
                    version,
                    count,

                            "recovery chain segment index does not match "
                            "the authenticated chain"
                        )

            finally:
                cls._release_chain_lock(fd)

@classmethod
    def _read_recovery_progress(
        cls, progress_path: str
    ) -> tuple[int, int, str, int, str, str, str] | None:
        """Read and strictly validate a resumable-build progress
        document, returning its binding -- ``(segment_size, boundary,
        boundary_digest, frames, head, prefix_digest, index_digest)``
        -- or ``None`` when the file is missing, truncated or defective
        in any way, which the caller treats as a one-shot rebuild from
        the canonical chain.

        A genuinely missing file is the normal first-build case and
        yields ``None``; every other open or read failure propagates as
        :class:`OSError`. The document binds the segment size, the last
        complete-segment boundary and its frame digest, the
        authenticated frame count and head, the SHA-256 of the prefix's
        canonical frame bytes through that boundary and the SHA-256 of
        the matching segment index's exact bytes; it never carries
        audit bodies.
        """
        try:
            with open(progress_path, "rb") as handle:
                raw = handle.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        if raw.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
            return None
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
            document = json.loads(
                text, object_pairs_hook=cls._reject_duplicate_json_keys
            )
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
            return None
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            return None
        if set(document.keys()) != set(cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_KEYS):
            return None
        if document["format"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT:
            return None
        version = document["version"]
        if (
            isinstance(version, bool)
            or not isinstance(version, int)
            or version
            not in cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS
        ):
            return None
        segment_size = document["segment_size"]
        boundary = document["boundary"]
        frames = document["frames"]
        for value in (segment_size, boundary, frames):
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
                return None
        if segment_size < 1 or boundary < 0 or frames < 1:
            return None
        if boundary % segment_size or boundary > frames:
            return None
        if frames - boundary >= segment_size:
            return None
        for name in (
            "boundary_digest",
            "head",
            "prefix_digest",
            "index_digest",
        ):
            value = document[name]
            if (
                not isinstance(value, str)
                or len(value) != 64
                or set(value) - cls._HEX_DIGITS
            ):
                return None
        if boundary == 0 and (
            document["boundary_digest"] != cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_GENESIS_PREV
        ):
            return None
        return (
            segment_size,
            boundary,
            document["boundary_digest"],
            frames,
            document["head"],
            document["prefix_digest"],
            document["index_digest"],
        )

    @classmethod
    def _progress_bytes(
        cls,
        segment_size: int,
        boundary: int,
        boundary_digest: str,
        frames: int,
        head: str,
        prefix_digest: str,
        index_digest: str,
    ) -> bytes:
        """Deterministic compact JSON for a progress binding: UTF-8
        without a BOM, no whitespace and no trailing newline, identical
        byte for byte for identical bindings."""

            "format": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_FORMAT,
            "version": cls._RECOVERY_CHAIN_PROGRESS_VERSION,
            "segment_size": segment_size,
            "boundary": boundary,
            "boundary_digest": boundary_digest,
            "frames": frames,
            "head": head,
            "prefix_digest": prefix_digest,
            "index_digest": index_digest,

    def _publish_files_rollback(
        cls,

    ) -> None:
        """Durably publish ``(temporary, target)`` pairs under a
        rollback protocol; every temporary already sits in its
        target's directory, flushed and fsync-ed.

        Every pre-existing target is first moved aside to a unique
        same-directory backup; the temps are then replaced onto the
        targets one by one with a directory sync after each move. If
        any replace or directory sync fails, every already-installed
        target is restored byte for byte from its backup (or removed
        when there was no previous file), the remaining backups are
        restored or removed, every temporary and backup created by this
        call is cleaned up and the :class:`OSError` propagates -- so a
        failed publication leaves each previous target exactly as it
        was, never a partial set. On success the backups are removed
        and the directory is synced.

        if not publications:
            return
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(publications[0][1]))

        installed: list[str] = []

        def clean_up() -> None:
            for target in reversed(installed):
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(target)
                backup = backups.get(target)
                if backup is not None:
                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                        os.replace(backup, target)
            for backup in backups.values():
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.remove(backup)
            for _tmp, target in publications:
                # An unpublished temp may still be at its temp path; a
                # published one is gone after restore above.
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    pass
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                cls._fsync_directory(directory)

            for tmp, target in publications:
                if os.path.exists(target):
                    backup = (
                        target
                        + f".recovery-backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.bak"

                    backups[target] = backup
                os.replace(tmp, target)

                cls._fsync_directory(directory)
